issues.text: I follow the chain now: a name server that does not hold the name says which ones to ask next. But I stopped at the start of the chain: which name servers does the resolver ask first, and how does it know them? Not needed for the main idea, but the question stays open.
issues.fix: Add a short clause saying where the resolver's first question goes, or say explicitly that where the chain starts is not this lesson's point.
issues.quote: A resolver that does not hold a name asks name servers: one that does not hold it replies not with an address but with which name servers to ask next

issues.text: I read this sentence twice. The three 'it's point at different things (the name, the answer, the name again), and 'pointed elsewhere' only makes sense to me after reaching section 6.
issues.fix: Split into two sentences and replace each 'it' with 'the name' or 'the answer'; say 'where the record is changed when the name is given a new address' instead of 'pointed elsewhere'.
issues.quote: For every name there are name servers that hold its true answer, normally more than one so it survives a machine going down; that is also where it changes when the name is pointed elsewhere.

issues.text: Three actions and an embedded clause in one sentence; I re-read it to work out which laptop lands where.
issues.fix: Split into two sentences: first the change and the other network reaching the new machine, then your own laptop still landing on the old one.
issues.quote: You notice this when you point a name at a new machine, reach the new one from a machine on another network, whose resolver never held the old answer, and keep landing on the old one from your own laptop.

issues.text: The misconception label on q4 option d and q6 option d uses 'domain name' and 'server', words the lesson never uses; section 6 says 'One name equals one machine.' If the app shows this label after a wrong answer, I would not recognise it as the idea I was taught.
issues.fix: Change the misconception text on q4 d and q6 d to 'One name equals one machine.' to match section 6.
issues.quote: One domain name equals one server.

issues.text: 'both answer with one address' can be read as 'each answers with a single address' instead of 'with the same address'; I paused to decide which was meant before judging the option.
issues.fix: Write 'Since `lab` and `donhang-lab` answer with the same address, they have to be two separate machines.'
issues.quote: Since `lab` and `donhang-lab` both answer with one address, they have to be two separate machines.
